main_body: Rectangular loom frame seen straight on: top beam, warp-thread panel with a red/yellow checker weave band, bottom beam, and two thin legs below
top_band: Orange rows 10-11 with a tan band at rows 12-13. This is the face of the top beam, not a horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The column through the middle runs dark outline (row 9), orange (10-11), tan (12-13), grey-white warp threads (14-18), red/yellow checker (19-22), tan and orange beam (23-24), dark outline (25), then legs. The top and bottom beams read as vertical bands of the same tone family as the frame, with no foreshortened top surface. The side posts are flat vertical strips. The guide's red 'front elevation' and 'thin seat' examples match this structure. The 1-2 row cap is a rim only, with no eave shadow and no inset on the panel.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown that leans toward the wood, so it is not near-black. The wood beams have only about 3 steps (orange, tan, dark brown). The side posts and legs are flat single-colour fills. The thread panel and checker band add some pattern but little real grain, shading or per-element highlighting. Compared with the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and speckled texture, each tile carries only a few colours.
